title: Fixed Price vs Hourly Rate: How to Pay a Freelancer
h1: Fixed price vs hourly rate: how to pay a freelancer
description: Fixed-price and hourly pay compared for freelance work: budget certainty, flexibility, scope changes, quality incentives and when each model fits.
intro: When you hire a freelancer, one of the first decisions is how to pay: a fixed price for a defined piece of work, or an hourly rate for time spent. Each model shifts risk in a different direction. Fixed prices give you certainty about cost but need a clear scope. Hourly rates give flexibility but less certainty. This article explains how each works and how to choose.

faq.a: Neither is always cheaper. A fixed price is cheaper when the scope is clear, and hourly is cheaper when the work is small or uncertain.

faq.q: What if the work grows during the project?
faq.a: With a fixed price, changes usually need a new quote. With hourly pay, the cost rises with the time spent.

faq.q: How do I stop hourly costs getting out of hand?
faq.a: Set a maximum number of hours or a budget cap, and ask for regular time reports.
Yes. Many projects use a fixed price for the main deliverable and hourly rates for extras or ongoing support.
A monthly retainer for a set amount of work is a common middle ground.
